hook: This is a short, gentle entry built almost entirely around one conversation. The object is an ordinary graphing calculator recovered from a condemned school, and the fun lies in how it talks: all caps, barely any punctuation, and a personality that leaks through every reply. Go in expecting charm rather than dread.
whyItMatters: SCP-168 shows how little an entry needs to make a sapient object memorable: one interview, one short report, and a name scratched inside a casing. It works as a counterweight to the many files where talking objects are threats to be managed. It is also a neat case of containment procedures being shaped by what an anomaly wants rather than by how dangerous it is.
thingsToNotice: Read the containment procedures again after the interview, and the window requirement turns into a small punchline. The calculator's slowness on harder sums suggests it is working the problems out by hand, like a child at a desk, which quietly ties it back to the boy whose name is in the case. Its questions about where Eric went give the piece a faint melancholy underneath the jokes. The overturned table in the follow-up report is the only real incident in the file, and it reads more like a sulk than a breach.

related.note: Another aging piece of hardware with a mind of its own, though with a far colder temperament.
A sapient anomaly whose interviews slowly turn suspicion into trust.
